## Networks

### buildNetwork {#buildNetwork}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function buildNetwork(input: BuildNetworkInput): Promise<Network>;
```

Build a transport network from an OpenStreetMap extract, zero or more GTFS feeds and an optional elevation raster, given as the bytes of the files. Loads the WebAssembly module first if needed. Rejects when a file cannot be read, and when a GTFS feed has errors of priority `HIGH`.

```js
const net = await peabiru.buildNetwork({ pbf, gtfs, nThreads: 2 });
console.log(net.info(), net.workers);
net.free();
```

Compatibility with r5r: `build_network()` with `elevation`, from bytes rather than a directory (the feeds load in array order, where r5r uses the order the operating system lists its directory; no `verbose`, `temp_dir` or `overwrite`; nothing is written to disk); `nThreads` is peabiru's own.

### BuildNetworkInput {#BuildNetworkInput}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface BuildNetworkInput
```

The input of `buildNetwork()`.

- `pbf: Bytes`: The OpenStreetMap extract: the bytes of a `.pbf` file.
- `gtfs?: GtfsFeed[]`: The GTFS feeds, loaded in this order (default: none, a street network only). A feed with errors of priority `HIGH` (see `getGtfsErrors()`) is refused: the build rejects with an `Error` naming it.
- `tif?: Bytes`: An elevation raster, the bytes of a GeoTIFF file (default: none): walking and cycling times then get the slope costs of `elevation`. One band, north up, uncompressed or compressed with LZW, Deflate or PackBits, in WGS 84 longitude and latitude (EPSG:4326), SIRGAS 2000 (4674), SAD69 (4618), Corrego Alegre (4225), their UTM zones used in Brazil, SIRGAS 2000 / Brazil Polyconic (5880), WGS 84 / UTM (326xx, 327xx) or Pseudo-Mercator (3857); other rasters are an error. Voids and values beyond +/-3276.7 m are stored wrapped around, as 16-bit decimetres, with a warning; in a projected raster, a street point within nanometres of a pixel boundary reads the pixel Java's StrictMath gives, with a warning. With a raster, `travelTimeMatrix()` never routes walking trips from the destinations.
- `elevation?: string`: The slope cost function when `tif` is given: `"TOBLER"` (default, Tobler's hiking function), `"MINETTI"` (Minetti's energy cost of walking) or `"NONE"`, in any case. Without `tif` it is `"NONE"`.
- `onWarning?: WarningHandler`: Receives the warnings of the build (about the raster); by default `console.warn`.
- `nThreads?: number | null`: Workers to route on. `1` (default): no workers, everything runs on the calling thread. A whole number above 1: a pool of that many workers (Web Workers in browsers, `worker_threads` in Node), each holding its own copy of the network, all built at once. `0`, `null` or `Infinity`: one worker per core (`navigator.hardwareConcurrency`, or Node's `os.availableParallelism()`). Each worker costs about the memory of a network built on the calling thread.
- `useWorkers?: boolean`: Route in workers even with one thread, so that a call never blocks the calling thread and can be aborted (default: `true` when `nThreads` is given and is not 1, else `false`; must not be `false` with more than one thread).

### GtfsFeed {#GtfsFeed}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface GtfsFeed
```

One GTFS feed: the `.zip` file's name and its bytes.

- `name: string`: The file name, such as `"poa_eptc.zip"`. It names the feed in messages and, when the feed has no `feed_info.feed_id`, gives its feed id (the name without `.zip`), which prefixes its stop ids. Names must be distinct.
- `data: Bytes`: The bytes of the `.zip` file.

### Bytes {#Bytes}

*type*

```typescript
export type Bytes = Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView;
```

Bytes of a file.

### WarningHandler {#WarningHandler}

*type*

```typescript
export type WarningHandler = (message: string) => void;
```

Receives each warning, as a string; by default `console.warn`.

### Network {#Network}

*class*

```typescript
export declare class Network
```

A transport network: the street network and, when GTFS feeds were given, the public transport layer, held in the memory of the WebAssembly module (or, for a network with workers, in each worker) until `free()`. Built by `buildNetwork()`; it cannot be sent to another Worker (build it there).

```js
console.log(network.info().stops, "stops,", network.workers, "workers");
console.log(await network.transitAvailability("2019-05-13"));
network.free();
```

- `free(): void`: Release the network's memory and stop its workers; calls still running on them reject. The network cannot be used afterwards. In Node, idle workers do not keep a program alive, so a program may also end without calling it.
- `readonly workers: number`: Number of workers of the network; 0 when it routes on the calling thread.
- `info(): NetworkInfo`: The sizes of the network (see [`NetworkInfo`](#NetworkInfo)).
- `transitAvailability(date: Date | string): Promise<{ services: number; active: number }>`: The number of services in the network and of those running on `date` (a Date, read in local time, or a string `"YYYY-MM-DD"`): the check the routing functions make on their departure date.
- `buildWarnings(): string[]`: The warnings of the build, which `buildNetwork()` also hands to `onWarning`: those about the elevation raster (samples stored wrapped around, beyond +/-3276.7 m, such as SRTM's -32768 voids, or equal to the raster's no-data value; street points near a pixel boundary of a projected raster).
- `r5rWarnings(): string[]`: The same as `buildWarnings()`, its name before version 0.1.0.

@deprecated Use `buildWarnings()`; this alias returns the same list.

### NetworkInfo {#NetworkInfo}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface NetworkInfo
```

Sizes of a network, from `network.info()`.

- `vertices: number`: Street vertices, including those of the connectors of transit stops.
- `edges: number`: Directed street edges, including the connectors of transit stops.
- `elevation: string`: The slope cost function in use: `"TOBLER"`, `"MINETTI"` or `"NONE"`.
- `feeds: string[]`: The GTFS feed ids, in loading order.
- `stops: number`: Transit stops.
- `patterns: number`: Trip patterns.
- `services: number`: GTFS services (calendars).
- `frequencies: boolean`: Whether any trip is frequency-based.

## Travel-time matrices

### travelTimeMatrix {#travelTimeMatrix}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function travelTimeMatrix(
  network: Network,
  origins: Points,
  destinations: Points,
  options?: TravelTimeMatrixOptions,
): Promise<TravelTimeMatrix>;
```

Travel times between every origin and every destination: on the streets by one mode, or by public transport with the percentiles of the travel times over the departure window (and, for frequency-based trips, over the Monte Carlo draws). Every option is in [`TravelTimeMatrixOptions`](#TravelTimeMatrixOptions) and [`RoutingOptions`](#RoutingOptions). Pairs not reached within `maxTripDuration` are left out.

```js
const ttm = await peabiru.travelTimeMatrix(network, points, points, {
  mode: ["WALK", "TRANSIT"],
  departureDatetime: "2019-05-13 14:00:00",
  percentiles: [25, 50, 75],
  seed: 42,
});
console.log(ttm.from_id[1], ttm.to_id[1], ttm.travel_time_p50[1]);
```

Compatibility with r5r: `travel_time_matrix()`, the same options in camelCase, defaults and result columns; `outputDir` is not supported.

### TravelTimeMatrixOptions {#TravelTimeMatrixOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TravelTimeMatrixOptions extends RoutingOptions
```

Options of `travelTimeMatrix()`.

Also takes every option of [`RoutingOptions`](#RoutingOptions).

- `departureDatetime?: DateTime | null`: Required with public transport; the current time otherwise (default null).
- `timeWindow?: number`: Minutes of departure times, from `departureDatetime` on (default 10).
- `percentiles?: number | number[]`: 1 to 5 distinct whole numbers from 1 to 99 (default 50): the percentiles of the travel times over the window.
- `fareStructure?: FareStructure | null`: A fare structure (see `setupFareStructure()`), or null (default): no fares. With one, public transport is routed with R5's multi-criteria router (McRAPTOR) over `timeWindow * drawsPerMinute` sampled departure times.
- `maxFare?: number`: The highest fare of a trip (default Infinity); a finite value needs a `fareStructure`.

### TravelTimeMatrix {#TravelTimeMatrix}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TravelTimeMatrix
```

Columns of a travel-time matrix: one row per origin and destination reached, origin-major in input order. `travel_time_pXX` (one per percentile, ascending, two digits: `travel_time_p05`) holds whole minutes, [`NA_INT32`](#NA_INT32) where a percentile is not reached.

- `from_id: (string | null)[]`
- `to_id: (string | null)[]`
- `` [travelTime: `travel_time_p${string}`]: Int32Array ``

## Accessibility

### accessibility {#accessibility}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function accessibility(
  network: Network,
  origins: Points,
  destinations: Points,
  options?: AccessibilityOptions,
): Promise<AccessibilityTable>;
```

Access to opportunities from each origin: the opportunities of the destinations (the columns `opportunitiesColnames`), weighted by a decay function of the travel time to them and summed. Every option is in [`AccessibilityOptions`](#AccessibilityOptions), [`TravelTimeMatrixOptions`](#TravelTimeMatrixOptions) and [`RoutingOptions`](#RoutingOptions).

```js
const access = await peabiru.accessibility(network, points, points, {
  opportunitiesColnames: "jobs",
  mode: "WALK",
  cutoffs: [10, 20],
});
console.log(access.id, access.cutoff, access.accessibility);
```

Compatibility with r5r: `accessibility()`, the same options in camelCase, defaults, decay functions and result columns (R5's exponential as Apache Commons Math computes it); `outputDir` is not supported.

### AccessibilityOptions {#AccessibilityOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface AccessibilityOptions extends TravelTimeMatrixOptions
```

Options of `accessibility()`.

Also takes every option of [`TravelTimeMatrixOptions`](#TravelTimeMatrixOptions).

- `opportunitiesColnames?: string | string[]`: Opportunity columns of the destinations (default `"opportunities"`). Missing values count as 0, with a warning.
- `decayFunction?: "step" | "exponential" | "fixed_exponential" | "linear" | "logistic"`: `"step"` (default), `"exponential"`, `"fixed_exponential"`, `"linear"` or `"logistic"`.
- `cutoffs?: number | number[] | null`: 1 to 12 distinct whole minutes from 1 to 120: the cutoffs of `"step"`, and for the other functions the travel time at which the weight is one half; null (default) only with `"fixed_exponential"`, which takes none.
- `decayValue?: number | null`: The decay constant (`"fixed_exponential"`, between 0 and 1), the width in whole minutes (`"linear"`, 1 to 59) or the standard deviation in minutes (`"logistic"`, at least 1); null (default) otherwise.

### AccessibilityTable {#AccessibilityTable}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface AccessibilityTable
```

Columns of an accessibility table: one row per origin, opportunity, percentile and cutoff, in that order. No `cutoff` with `"fixed_exponential"`.

- `id: (string | null)[]`
- `opportunity: string[]`
- `percentile: Int32Array`
- `cutoff?: Int32Array`
- `accessibility: Float64Array`

## Expanded and arrival matrices

### expandedTravelTimeMatrix {#expandedTravelTimeMatrix}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function expandedTravelTimeMatrix(
  network: Network,
  origins: Points,
  destinations: Points,
  options?: ExpandedTravelTimeMatrixOptions,
): Promise<ExpandedMatrix>;
```

Travel times by public transport minute by minute: one row per origin, destination, departure minute of the window and Monte Carlo draw, instead of percentiles, with the routes taken and, with `breakdown`, the parts of each trip. Every option is in [`ExpandedTravelTimeMatrixOptions`](#ExpandedTravelTimeMatrixOptions) and [`RoutingOptions`](#RoutingOptions). A street mode alone throws [`UnsupportedError`](#UnsupportedError) (use `travelTimeMatrix()`).

```js
const etm = await peabiru.expandedTravelTimeMatrix(network, points, points, {
  mode: ["WALK", "TRANSIT"],
  departureDatetime: "2019-05-13 14:00:00",
  timeWindow: 2,
  seed: 42,
  breakdown: true,
});
console.log(etm.departure_time[0], etm.routes[0], etm.total_time[0]);
```

Compatibility with r5r: `expanded_travel_time_matrix()`, the same options in camelCase, defaults and result columns; with a street mode alone r5r answers with one trip from a departure time taken from the clock, where peabiru throws; `outputDir` is not supported.

### arrivalTravelTimeMatrix {#arrivalTravelTimeMatrix}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function arrivalTravelTimeMatrix(
  network: Network,
  origins: Points,
  destinations: Points,
  options: ArrivalTravelTimeMatrixOptions,
): Promise<ExpandedMatrix>;
```

The latest trip by public transport that arrives by `arrivalDatetime`, for each origin and destination: the departures of the `maxTripDuration` minutes before it are searched, and each pair keeps the one that leaves last and arrives in time. The columns are those of `expandedTravelTimeMatrix()`. Every option is in [`ArrivalTravelTimeMatrixOptions`](#ArrivalTravelTimeMatrixOptions) and [`RoutingOptions`](#RoutingOptions). A street mode alone throws [`UnsupportedError`](#UnsupportedError).

```js
const atm = await peabiru.arrivalTravelTimeMatrix(network, points, points, {
  mode: ["WALK", "TRANSIT"],
  arrivalDatetime: "2019-05-13 15:00:00",
  seed: 42,
});
console.log(atm.from_id[0], atm.to_id[0], atm.departure_time[0], atm.total_time[0]);
```

Compatibility with r5r: `arrival_travel_time_matrix()`, the same options in camelCase, defaults and result columns; peabiru throws with a street mode alone; `outputDir` is not supported.

### ExpandedTravelTimeMatrixOptions {#ExpandedTravelTimeMatrixOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface ExpandedTravelTimeMatrixOptions extends RoutingOptions
```

Options of `expandedTravelTimeMatrix()`.

Also takes every option of [`RoutingOptions`](#RoutingOptions).

- `departureDatetime?: DateTime | null`: Required: the first departure time.
- `timeWindow?: number`: Minutes of departure times, from `departureDatetime` on (default 10).
- `breakdown?: boolean`: Break each trip down into its parts (default false).

### ArrivalTravelTimeMatrixOptions {#ArrivalTravelTimeMatrixOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface ArrivalTravelTimeMatrixOptions extends RoutingOptions
```

Options of `arrivalTravelTimeMatrix()`.

Also takes every option of [`RoutingOptions`](#RoutingOptions).

- `arrivalDatetime: DateTime`: Required: the time by which trips must arrive.
- `breakdown?: boolean`: Break each trip down into its parts (default false).

### ExpandedMatrix {#ExpandedMatrix}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface ExpandedMatrix
```

Columns of an expanded or arrival matrix: times are minutes with one decimal, `NaN` for trips longer than `maxTripDuration` (whose `routes` are null and `n_rides` [`NA_INT32`](#NA_INT32)). `departure_time` is `"HH:MM:SS"` (hours not wrapped at 24); `draw_number` counts the draws of a departure minute from 1; `routes` holds the route ids of the rides joined by `"|"`, or `"[WALK]"` for a trip on foot. The breakdown columns are present only with `breakdown: true`.

- `from_id: (string | null)[]`
- `to_id: (string | null)[]`
- `departure_time: string[]`
- `draw_number: Int32Array`
- `access_time?: Float64Array`
- `wait_time?: Float64Array`
- `ride_time?: Float64Array`
- `transfer_time?: Float64Array`
- `egress_time?: Float64Array`
- `routes: (string | null)[]`
- `n_rides?: Int32Array`
- `total_time: Float64Array`

## Detailed itineraries

### detailedItineraries {#detailedItineraries}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function detailedItineraries(
  network: Network,
  origins: Points,
  destinations: Points,
  options?: DetailedItinerariesOptions,
): Promise<{ type: "FeatureCollection"; features: ItineraryFeature[] } | ItineraryRow[]>;
```

The legs of the trips between pairs of origins and destinations: each walk, ride by bicycle or car and public transport ride, with its duration, wait, distance, route and line. Each pair gets its fastest itinerary over the departure window (the trip by the street mode alone, or by public transport, whichever is faster) or, with `shortestPath: false`, the alternatives found by R5's multi-criteria router (McRAPTOR). One row per leg, as a GeoJSON [`FeatureCollection`](#FeatureCollection) or, with `dropGeometry`, an array of rows; pairs without an itinerary have none. Every option is in [`DetailedItinerariesOptions`](#DetailedItinerariesOptions) and [`RoutingOptions`](#RoutingOptions). Public transport needs feeds with timetables: a network with frequency-based trips is an error. With `modeEgress: "CAR"`, a pair whose itinerary in r5r may depend on the searches that ran before (a car search through a turn restriction with two or more via ways) gets r5r's itinerary on a fresh network, with a warning.

```js
const back = { id: [...points.id].reverse(), lon: [...points.lon].reverse(), lat: [...points.lat].reverse() };
const legs = await peabiru.detailedItineraries(network, points, back, {
  mode: "BICYCLE",
  departureDatetime: "2019-05-13 14:00:00",
  dropGeometry: true,
});
console.log(legs.map((r) => `${r.from_id} > ${r.to_id}: ${r.total_duration} min, ${r.total_distance} m`));
```

Compatibility with r5r: `detailed_itineraries()`, the same options in camelCase, defaults, rows and lines (GeoJSON for r5r's `sf`), with the refusals above; `outputDir` is not supported.

### DetailedItinerariesOptions {#DetailedItinerariesOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface DetailedItinerariesOptions extends Omit<RoutingOptions, "drawsPerMinute" | "seed">
```

Options of `detailedItineraries()`.

- `departureDatetime?: DateTime | null`: Required with public transport; the current time otherwise.
- `timeWindow?: number`: Minutes of departure times, from `departureDatetime` on (default 10).
- `suboptimalMinutes?: number`: With `shortestPath: false`, how many minutes after the best arrival at a stop the multi-criteria search still keeps a state there, which widens the set of alternatives (default 0). Must be 0 with `shortestPath: true` or a `fareStructure`.
- `shortestPath?: boolean`: Only the fastest itinerary of each pair (default true); `false` gives the alternatives, one per sequence of routes.
- `allToAll?: boolean`: Route from every origin to every destination (default false: pair them row by row, a single origin or destination repeated to match the other).
- `fareStructure?: FareStructure | null`: A fare structure (default null): trips routed with fares, and fare columns in the result.
- `maxFare?: number`: The highest fare of a trip (default Infinity); a finite value needs a `fareStructure`.
- `dropGeometry?: boolean`: Plain rows instead of GeoJSON features (default false).
- `osmLinkIds?: boolean`: Add the properties `osm_id_list`, `edge_id_list`, `board_stop_id` and `alight_stop_id` to each row (default false; needs `dropGeometry: false`): see [`ItineraryRow`](#ItineraryRow).

### ItineraryRow {#ItineraryRow}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface ItineraryRow
```

One leg of an itinerary: durations and waits are minutes with one decimal, distances metres; `route` is the GTFS `route_id` of a ride, empty for a street leg.

- `from_id: string | null`
- `from_lat: number`
- `from_lon: number`
- `to_id: string | null`
- `to_lat: number`
- `to_lon: number`
- `option: number`: The itinerary of the pair, from 1.
- `departure_time: string`: `"HH:MM:SS"`, when the itinerary leaves the origin.
- `total_duration: number`
- `total_distance: number`
- `total_fare?: number`: With a fare structure only.
- `segment: number`: The leg, from 1.
- `mode: string`: `"WALK"`, `"BICYCLE"`, `"CAR"`, or the mode of a ride, such as `"BUS"`.
- `cumulative_fare?: number`: With a fare structure only: the fare paid up to the end of the leg.
- `segment_duration: number`
- `wait: number`
- `distance: number`
- `route: string`
- `osm_id_list?: string`: With `osmLinkIds`: the OpenStreetMap way ids of a street leg's edges, as `"[id1, id2, ...]"` (`"[]"` for a ride; consecutive edges on a roundabout give only their first ids, connectors none).
- `edge_id_list?: string`: With `osmLinkIds`: the indices of those edges in the street network (`edge_index` of `streetNetworkToSf()`), as `"[i1, i2, ...]"`.
- `board_stop_id?: string`: With `osmLinkIds`: a ride's boarding stop, `"<feed>:<stop_id>"`; empty for street legs.
- `alight_stop_id?: string`: With `osmLinkIds`: a ride's alighting stop, `"<feed>:<stop_id>"`; empty for street legs.

### ItineraryFeature {#ItineraryFeature}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface ItineraryFeature
```

A leg with its line (longitude, latitude), as a GeoJSON feature.

- `type: "Feature"`
- `properties: ItineraryRow`
- `geometry: { type: "LineString"; coordinates: [number, number][] }`

## Fares

### setupFareStructure {#setupFareStructure}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function setupFareStructure(
  network: Network,
  baseFare: number,
  options?: SetupFareStructureOptions,
): Promise<FareStructure>;
```

A fare structure for the routes of a network in which every route, fare type and transfer between two types costs `baseFare` (at least 0, read as a 32-bit float), with one fare type per mode, per agency or for all routes (`by`). Edit its columns to set other fares.

```js
const fares = await peabiru.setupFareStructure(network, 4.4);
console.log(fares.fares_per_type.type, fares.fares_per_route.route_id.length, "routes");
```

Compatibility with r5r: `setup_fare_structure()`, the same structure (with objects of columns for r5r's `data.table`s).

### SetupFareStructureOptions {#SetupFareStructureOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface SetupFareStructureOptions
```

Options of `setupFareStructure()`.

- `by?: string`: One fare type per mode (`"MODE"`, the default), per agency (`"AGENCY_ID"`, `"AGENCY_NAME"`) or one for all routes (`"GENERIC"`).
- `debugPath?: string | null`: A `.csv` path, kept in `debug_settings` (default null).
- `debugInfo?: string | null`: `"MODE"`, `"ROUTE"` (the default with a `debugPath`) or `"MODE_ROUTE"`, kept in `debug_settings`; needs a `debugPath`.

### FareStructure {#FareStructure}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface FareStructure
```

A fare structure: the global settings, three tables as objects of columns, and the debug settings. Made by `setupFareStructure()` or read by `readFareStructure()`, and changed by editing its columns.

- `max_discounted_transfers: number | null`: Most transfers with a discount (default 1; null for none).
- `transfer_time_allowance: number | null`: Minutes between the boardings of a discounted transfer (default 120).
- `fare_cap: number`: Highest fare of a trip (Infinity: no cap).
- `fares_per_type: { type: (string | null)[]; unlimited_transfers: boolean[]; allow_same_route_transfer: boolean[]; use_route_fare: boolean[]; fare: number[]; }`: One row per fare type: its name, whether its transfers are unlimited, whether a transfer to the same route is allowed, whether the route's own fare is used, and its fare.
- `fares_per_transfer: { first_leg: (string | null)[]; second_leg: (string | null)[]; fare: number[] }`: The fare of two rides together, for the pairs of fare types with a discount.
- `fares_per_route: { agency_id: (string | null)[]; agency_name: (string | null)[]; route_id: (string | null)[]; route_short_name: (string | null)[]; route_long_name: (string | null)[]; mode: (string | null)[]; route_fare: number[]; fare_type: (string | null)[]; }`: The fare type of each GTFS route, matched by `agency_id` and `route_id`; a route of the network missing from it is an error.
- `debug_settings: { output_file: string; trip_info: string }`: Kept as given; no debug file is written.

### readFareStructure {#readFareStructure}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function readFareStructure(
  bytes: Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView,
  encoding?: "UTF-8" | "unknown" | "Latin-1",
): FareStructure;
```

A fare structure read from the bytes of a `.zip` file of fare structure CSV files (written by `writeFareStructure()`, for example), whose text is in `encoding`: `"UTF-8"` (default), `"Latin-1"` or `"unknown"`. Synchronous; needs the module loaded (`init()` or `buildNetwork()` first).

```js
const bytes = peabiru.writeFareStructure(await peabiru.setupFareStructure(network, 4.4));
const fares = peabiru.readFareStructure(bytes);
console.log(fares.fare_cap, fares.fares_per_type.fare);
```

Compatibility with r5r: `read_fare_structure()`, from the file's bytes rather than a path; it reads r5r's files.

### writeFareStructure {#writeFareStructure}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function writeFareStructure(fareStructure: FareStructure): Uint8Array;
```

The bytes of a fare structure `.zip` file: one CSV file for the global settings and one per table, deflated as r5r's are. Synchronous; needs the module loaded. Throws when the structure is not one.

```js
const bytes = peabiru.writeFareStructure(await peabiru.setupFareStructure(network, 4.4));
console.log(bytes.length, "bytes"); // in Node: await writeFile("fares.zip", bytes)
```

Compatibility with r5r: `write_fare_structure()`, the same CSV files (r5r reads them), returned as bytes rather than written to a path; the archive's bytes differ, since r5r's also holds file dates.

### paretoFrontier {#paretoFrontier}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function paretoFrontier(
  network: Network,
  origins: Points,
  destinations: Points,
  options?: ParetoFrontierOptions,
): Promise<ParetoFrontierTable>;
```

The trade-off between travel time and fare: for each origin, destination and percentile, the travel time within each fare cutoff, one row per cutoff at which it changes. Routed with R5's multi-criteria router (McRAPTOR) over one departure time per minute of the window. Every option is in [`ParetoFrontierOptions`](#ParetoFrontierOptions) and [`RoutingOptions`](#RoutingOptions).

```js
const frontier = await peabiru.paretoFrontier(network, points, points, {
  departureDatetime: "2019-05-13 14:00:00",
  fareStructure: await peabiru.setupFareStructure(network, 4.4),
  fareCutoffs: [0, 4.4, 8.8],
  seed: 42,
});
console.log(frontier.from_id.length, "rows", frontier.monetary_cost[0]);
```

Compatibility with r5r: `pareto_frontier()`, the same options in camelCase, defaults and result columns; `outputDir` is not supported.

### ParetoFrontierOptions {#ParetoFrontierOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface ParetoFrontierOptions extends Omit<RoutingOptions, "drawsPerMinute" | "newCarspeeds" | "carspeedScale" | "newLts">
```

Options of `paretoFrontier()`.

- `mode?: string | string[]`: As in the other functions, but `["WALK", "TRANSIT"]` by default.
- `departureDatetime?: DateTime | null`: Required with public transport.
- `timeWindow?: number`: Minutes of departure times, from `departureDatetime` on (default 10), sampled once a minute.
- `percentiles?: number | number[]`: 1 to 5 distinct whole numbers from 1 to 99 (default 50).
- `fareStructure?: FareStructure`: Required: the fare structure.
- `fareCutoffs?: number | number[]`: Required: the fare cutoffs, at least 0, distinct.

### ParetoFrontierTable {#ParetoFrontierTable}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface ParetoFrontierTable
```

Columns of a Pareto frontier: one row per origin, destination, percentile and fare cutoff at which the travel time changes. `monetary_cost` is the cutoff as R5 reads it, a 32-bit float (4.4 is 4.400000095367432).

- `from_id: (string | null)[]`
- `to_id: (string | null)[]`
- `percentile: Int32Array`
- `travel_time: Int32Array`
- `monetary_cost: Float64Array`

## Isochrones

### isochrone {#isochrone}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function isochrone(
  network: Network,
  origins: Points,
  options: IsochroneOptions & { polygonOutput: false },
): Promise<FeatureCollection<LineString, IsochroneLineProperties>>;
export declare function isochrone(
  network: Network,
  origins: Points,
  options?: IsochroneOptions,
): Promise<FeatureCollection<MultiPolygon, IsochronePolygonProperties>>;
```

The areas, or the street segments, reached from each origin within each cutoff. With `polygonOutput: true` (the default), one [`MultiPolygon`](#MultiPolygon) feature per origin, percentile (ascending) and cutoff (descending), empty when nothing is reached, made by interpolating the travel times on a Web Mercator grid (`zoom`) and tracing their contours with isoband's algorithm; with `polygonOutput: false`, one [`LineString`](#LineString) per street segment reached, by origin, then band and travel time descending. Every option is in [`IsochroneOptions`](#IsochroneOptions).

```js
const iso = await peabiru.isochrone(network, points, {
  mode: "WALK",
  cutoffs: [5, 10],
});
console.log(iso.features.map((f) => `${f.properties.id} ${f.properties.isochrone} min`));
```

Compatibility with r5r: `isochrone()`, the same options in camelCase, defaults and properties; the polygons are those r5r makes before `sf::st_make_valid()`, which is not applied (the same areas, not snapped to 1e-7 degrees, always MultiPolygons), with their rings in the order isoband gives on macOS on every platform.

### IsochroneOptions {#IsochroneOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface IsochroneOptions extends Omit<RoutingOptions, "newCarspeeds" | "carspeedScale" | "newLts" | "outputDir" | "maxTripDuration">
```

Options of `isochrone()`: those of the routing functions (no fares, scenarios or `outputDir`), plus its own.

- `mode?: string | string[]`: As in the other functions, but `"transit"` by default (case does not matter).
- `modeEgress?: string`: `"walk"` by default (case does not matter).
- `cutoffs?: number | number[]`: Minutes that delimit the isochrones (default `[0, 15, 30]`): finite and at least 0, sorted and made distinct, 0 added; one must be above 0. The largest is the trip limit.
- `zoom?: number`: Web Mercator zoom level, 9 to 12, of the grid the polygons are made from (default 10).
- `polygonOutput?: boolean`: `true` (default) for polygons, `false` for the street segments reached.
- `departureDatetime?: DateTime | null`: Required with public transport; the current time otherwise (default null).
- `timeWindow?: number`: Minutes of departure times, from `departureDatetime` on (default 10).
- `percentiles?: number | number[] | null`: 1 to 5 distinct values from 1 to 99: one set of polygons per percentile; null (default) means 50. Must be null for lines.
- `maxTripDuration?: number`: Accepted and not used: the trip limit comes from the cutoffs.
- `sampleSize?: unknown`: Deprecated and not used: giving it only warns.

### IsochronePolygonProperties {#IsochronePolygonProperties}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface IsochronePolygonProperties
```

Properties of a polygon isochrone.

- `id: string | null`
- `isochrone: number`: The cutoff, minutes.
- `percentile: string`: Such as `"p50"`.

### IsochroneLineProperties {#IsochroneLineProperties}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface IsochroneLineProperties
```

Properties of a line isochrone: the street segment, with the properties of [`StreetEdgeProperties`](#StreetEdgeProperties).

- `id: string | null`
- `edge_index: string`: The directed edge index, as a string.
- `osm_id: number`
- `isochrone: number`: The smallest cutoff at or above the travel time, minutes.
- `travel_time_p50: number`: The travel time to the segment, minutes.
- `from_vertex: number`
- `to_vertex: number`
- `street_class: "MOTORWAY" | "PRIMARY" | "SECONDARY" | "TERTIARY" | "OTHER"`
- `length: number`: Metres.
- `walk: boolean`
- `car: boolean`
- `car_speed: number`: km/h.
- `bicycle: boolean`
- `bicycle_lts: number`

### FeatureCollection {#FeatureCollection}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface FeatureCollection<G, P>
```

A GeoJSON FeatureCollection.

- `type: "FeatureCollection"`
- `features: Feature<G, P>[]`

### Feature {#Feature}

*interface*

```typescript

```

A GeoJSON feature (coordinates `[lon, lat]`, WGS 84).

- `type: "Feature"`
- `properties: P`
- `geometry: G`

*interface*


A GeoJSON MultiPolygon: polygons of rings (shell first, then holes), every ring closed.

A GeoJSON LineString.

## Inspecting a network

### findSnap {#findSnap}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function findSnap(network: Network, points: Points, options?: FindSnapOptions): Promise<SnapTable>;
```

Where points snap to the street network: for each point, the nearest point of a street the mode may use, first within 300 metres and then within `radius`. A point that does not snap is not routed.

```js
const snap = await peabiru.findSnap(network, points, { mode: "CAR" });
console.log(snap.point_id, snap.distance, snap.found);
```

Compatibility with r5r: `find_snap()`, the same options, defaults and columns.

### FindSnapOptions {#FindSnapOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface FindSnapOptions
```

Options of `findSnap()`.

- `radius?: number`: The largest distance in metres within which to snap (default 1600).
- `mode?: "WALK" | "BICYCLE" | "CAR"`: The mode whose streets the points snap to (default `"WALK"`).
- `onWarning?: WarningHandler`: Receives the warnings about the points; by default `console.warn`.
- `signal?: AbortSignal`: Aborts the call.

### SnapTable {#SnapTable}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface SnapTable
```

Where points snap to the streets: one row per point.

- `point_id: (string | null)[]`
- `lat: Float64Array`
- `lon: Float64Array`
- `snap_lat: Float64Array`: Where the point snaps; NaN where it does not.
- `snap_lon: Float64Array`
- `distance: Float64Array`: Metres from the point to where it snaps (haversine on R5's sphere of radius 6,367,450 m); NaN where it does not snap.
- `found: boolean[]`

### streetNetworkBbox {#streetNetworkBbox}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function streetNetworkBbox(network: Network, output: "vector"): Promise<{ xmin: number; ymin: number; xmax: number; ymax: number }>;
export declare function streetNetworkBbox(network: Network, output: "bbox"): Promise<[number, number, number, number]>;
export declare function streetNetworkBbox(network: Network, output?: "polygon"): Promise<Polygon>;
```

The bounding box of the street network: R5's envelope of the street layer, which covers every OpenStreetMap node of the ways streets were made from. `output` is `"polygon"` (the default, a Polygon whose ring starts at the south-west corner and goes counter-clockwise), `"bbox"` (the GeoJSON bbox `[xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax]`) or `"vector"` (an object).

```js
console.log(await peabiru.streetNetworkBbox(network, "vector"));
```

Compatibility with r5r: `street_network_bbox()`, the same three outputs (GeoJSON for r5r's `sfc` and `bbox`, an object for its named vector).

### Polygon {#Polygon}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface Polygon
```

A GeoJSON Polygon: rings of `[lon, lat]`, shell first, every ring closed.

- `type: "Polygon"`
- `coordinates: [number, number][][]`

### Point {#Point}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface Point
```

A GeoJSON Point.

- `type: "Point"`
- `coordinates: [number, number]`

```typescript
  vertices: FeatureCollection<Point, StreetVertexProperties>;
  edges: FeatureCollection<LineString, StreetEdgeProperties>;

```

The street network as GeoJSON: `vertices`, the Points at the ends of street edges, and `edges`, every directed street edge as a LineString (the connectors of transit stops and park-and-rides left out), in the network's order.

```js
const { vertices, edges } = await peabiru.streetNetworkToSf(network);
console.log(vertices.features.length, edges.features.length, edges.features[0].properties);
```

Compatibility with r5r: `street_network_to_sf()`, the same features, properties and order (GeoJSON for r5r's two `sf` tables).

### StreetVertexProperties {#StreetVertexProperties}

Properties of a street vertex.

Properties of a directed street edge.

- `from_vertex: number`

### InspectOptions {#InspectOptions}

```typescript
export interface InspectOptions
```

Options of the functions that only read the network.

### transitNetworkToSf {#transitNetworkToSf}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function transitNetworkToSf(network: Network, options?: InspectOptions): Promise<{
  stops: FeatureCollection<Point | null, TransitStopProperties>;
  routes: FeatureCollection<LineString | Point, TransitRouteProperties>;
}>;
```

The public transport network as GeoJSON: `stops`, one Point per stop (a stop not linked to the streets has a null geometry), and `routes`, one feature per trip pattern, whose line is the GTFS shape of the trip that made the pattern or, without one, the positions of its linked stops. Patterns without a line are left out, and a line whose points are all the same is a Point.

```js
const { stops, routes } = await peabiru.transitNetworkToSf(network);
console.log(stops.features.length, "stops,", routes.features.length, "routes", routes.features[0].properties);
```

Compatibility with r5r: `transit_network_to_sf()`, the same features, properties and order (a null geometry for r5r's `POINT EMPTY`).

### TransitStopProperties {#TransitStopProperties}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TransitStopProperties
```

Properties of a transit stop.

- `stop_index: number`
- `stop_id: string`: Prefixed by the feed id (`feed:stop`).
- `stop_name: string | null`: null when blank.
- `linked_to_street: boolean`

### TransitRouteProperties {#TransitRouteProperties}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TransitRouteProperties
```

Properties of a transit route (one per trip pattern); null where blank.

- `agency_id: string | null`
- `agency_name: string | null`
- `route_id: string`
- `long_name: string | null`
- `short_name: string | null`
- `mode: string`: R5's mode of the GTFS `route_type`, such as `"BUS"`.

### checkTransitAvailability {#checkTransitAvailability}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function checkTransitAvailability(network: Network, options?: TransitAvailabilityOptions): Promise<TransitAvailabilityTable>;
```

The services active on dates: the given `dates`, every date from `startDate` to `endDate`, or, with no date option, the dates on which some trip runs, found from the network (ascending). `total_services` counts every service, used by trips or not.

```js
const week = await peabiru.checkTransitAvailability(network, { startDate: "2019-05-12", endDate: "2019-05-18" });
console.log(week.date, week.active_services);
```

Compatibility with r5r: `check_transit_availability()`, the same options and columns, with the dates as strings.

### TransitAvailabilityOptions {#TransitAvailabilityOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TransitAvailabilityOptions
```

Options of `checkTransitAvailability()`: none (discovery), `dates`, or `startDate` and `endDate`.

- `dates?: string | Date | Array<string | Date>`: Dates to check: `"YYYY-MM-DD"` strings or Dates (their local date).
- `startDate?: string | Date`: The first date of a range to check.
- `endDate?: string | Date`: The last date of a range to check.
- `signal?: AbortSignal`: Aborts the call.

### TransitAvailabilityTable {#TransitAvailabilityTable}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TransitAvailabilityTable
```

Services active on each date.

- `date: string[]`: `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.
- `total_services: Int32Array`

### getGtfsErrors {#getGtfsErrors}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function getGtfsErrors(feeds: GtfsFeed[] | { gtfs: GtfsFeed[] }): Promise<GtfsErrorsTable>;
```

The errors gtfs-lib (R5's GTFS library) reports when it loads GTFS feeds, one row per error, feed by feed in the order gtfs-lib finds them. A Network does not keep its feeds: pass them as `buildNetwork()` takes them (an array of `{name, data}`, or an object with a `gtfs` array). Loads the module first if needed. Rejects with an Error naming the cause for a feed on which gtfs-lib fails instead, and for a `locations.geojson` (GTFS-Flex zones) that is not in UTF-8. GTFS-Flex zones and location groups are read as gtfs-lib reads them, for its errors; on-demand trips are not routed.

```js
const errors = await peabiru.getGtfsErrors(gtfs);
console.log(errors.type.length, "errors:", [...new Set(errors.type)]);
```

Compatibility with r5r: `get_gtfs_errors()`, the same rows and columns, in a fixed order (r5r's changes from run to run), from the feeds' bytes rather than the network.

### GtfsErrorsTable {#GtfsErrorsTable}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface GtfsErrorsTable
```

The errors gtfs-lib reports in GTFS feeds: one row per error.

- `file: (string | null)[]`: The table, without `.txt`.
- `line: Int32Array`: The record, the header being line 1; 0 for a whole table.
- `type: string[]`: gtfs-lib's error class, such as `"DuplicateKeyError"`.
- `field: (string | null)[]`
- `id: (string | null)[]`: The key concerned, for duplicate keys and suspect stop locations.
- `priority: string[]`: `"HIGH"` (`buildNetwork()` refuses the feed), `"MEDIUM"`, `"LOW"` or `"UNKNOWN"`.

## Points, dates, scenarios and shared options

### Points {#Points}

*type*

```typescript
export type Points =
  | { id: ArrayLike<string | number | null>; lon: Numbers; lat: Numbers; [column: string]: unknown }
  | Array<{ id: string | number | null; lon: number | null; lat: number | null; [column: string]: unknown }>;
```

Points: columns `id`, `lon` and `lat` (WGS 84), or an array of `{id, lon, lat}` objects. Ids that are not strings are converted with `String()` (with a warning); points with missing coordinates (`null`, `NaN`) are not routed (with a warning); duplicated ids are an error. For `accessibility()`, the destinations also hold the opportunity columns (or properties).

### Numbers {#Numbers}

*type*

```typescript
export type Numbers = ArrayLike<number | null | undefined>;
```

Numbers as a plain array or any typed array.

### DateTime {#DateTime}

*type*

```typescript
export type DateTime = Date | string;
```

A date and clock time: a `Date` (its local date and clock time in the JavaScript runtime's time zone), or a string `"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"` (also with `T`, or without seconds), taken as it reads, which is the safer choice: the clock time of the GTFS feeds.

### RoutingOptions {#RoutingOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface RoutingOptions
```

Options shared by the routing functions, with their defaults.

- `mode?: string | string[]`: `"WALK"` (default), `"BICYCLE"` or `"CAR"` alone, or public transport: `"TRANSIT"` (every transit mode) or any of `"TRAM"`, `"SUBWAY"`, `"RAIL"`, `"BUS"`, `"FERRY"`, `"CABLE_CAR"`, `"GONDOLA"`, `"FUNICULAR"`, with at most one street mode to reach it (walking by default; by bicycle or car, the trip goes on on foot from where the vehicle is left). Case does not matter.
- `modeEgress?: string`: `"WALK"` (default), `"BICYCLE"` or `"CAR"`: from public transport to the destinations.
- `maxWalkTime?: number`: Minutes of walking, to or from public transport, or alone; `Infinity` (default) means the trip limit.
- `maxBikeTime?: number`: Minutes by bicycle, to or from public transport, or alone; `Infinity` (default) means the trip limit.
- `maxCarTime?: number`: Minutes by car, to or from public transport, or alone; `Infinity` (default) means the trip limit.
- `maxTripDuration?: number`: The longest trip, in whole minutes (default 120).
- `walkSpeed?: number`: Walking speed, km/h (default 3.6).
- `bikeSpeed?: number`: Cycling speed, km/h (default 12).
- `maxRides?: number`: Most public transport vehicles boarded in a trip (default 3).
- `maxLts?: number`: Highest level of traffic stress a cyclist rides on, 1 to 4 (default 2).
- `newCarspeeds?: ScenarioTable | GeoJsonFeatureCollection | null`: A scenario of car speeds (default null): a table (an object of columns or an array of rows) with `osm_id`, `max_speed` and `speed_type` (`"scale"`, a factor for the car speed of the way's edges, or `"km/h"`, a speed; 0 closes the way to cars), or a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of Polygons or MultiPolygons with properties `poly_id` (string), `scale` and `priority` (integer): each edge takes the factor of the polygon it meets with the highest priority (on a tie, the one it overlaps most). A speed that R5's 16-bit cm/s would bring to 0 or less is an error.
- `carspeedScale?: number`: The factor for the car speeds of the edges `newCarspeeds` leaves out, at least 0 (default 1).
- `newLts?: ScenarioTable | GeoJsonFeatureCollection | null`: A scenario of levels of traffic stress (default null): a table with `osm_id` and `lts` (integer, 1 to 4), or a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of LineStrings with properties `line_id`, `lts` (1 to 4) and `priority` (not used): each edge takes the level of the closest line among those whose bounding box meets its own. A scenario changes the street search from the origins but not the egress from the stops; on a network with elevation, a call with a scenario routes without slope costs, with a warning.
- `drawsPerMinute?: number`: Monte Carlo draws per departure minute for frequency-based GTFS (default 5).
- `seed?: number | null`: Seed of the Monte Carlo draws, an integer. With frequency-based GTFS the results are reproducible only with a seed; without one (null, the default) a random seed is drawn for each call.
- `nThreads?: number | null`: Workers of the network this call uses: a whole number >= 1, or null or Infinity (default) for all of them. More than the network has means all it has; a network without workers routes on the calling thread whatever this is. The origins are shared out in contiguous blocks, one per worker; the results do not depend on how.
- `signal?: AbortSignal | null`: Stops the call, which then rejects with the signal's reason (an `AbortError` `DOMException` for `controller.abort()`). On a network with workers, the call's workers are stopped at once and replaced, in the background, by new ones built from the same input; the network stays usable (later calls wait for the new workers). On the calling thread a running call cannot be interrupted: the signal is checked only before it starts.
- `verbose?: boolean`: Must be a boolean (default false); nothing is printed.
- `progress?: boolean`: Must be a boolean (default true); no progress is shown.
- `outputDir?: string | null`: Writing the results to files: must be null (default); anything else throws [`UnsupportedError`](#UnsupportedError).
- `onWarning?: WarningHandler`: Receives the warnings of the call; by default `console.warn`.

### ScenarioTable {#ScenarioTable}

*type*

```typescript
export type ScenarioTable = Record<string, ArrayLike<unknown>> | Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
```

A table of a scenario: an object of columns, or an array of row objects.

### GeoJsonFeatureCollection {#GeoJsonFeatureCollection}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface GeoJsonFeatureCollection
```

A GeoJSON FeatureCollection (WGS 84).

- `type: "FeatureCollection"`
- `features: Array<{ type: "Feature"; properties: Record<string, unknown>; geometry: { type: string; coordinates: unknown } }>`

## Missing values and errors

### NA_INT32 {#NA_INT32}

*constant*

```typescript
export declare const NA_INT32: -2147483648;
```

The missing value (NA) of the `Int32Array` columns of the results: -2147483648, the smallest 32-bit integer. The `Float64Array` columns use `NaN`, and the string columns `null`.

```js
const ttm = await peabiru.travelTimeMatrix(network, points, points, {
  mode: ["WALK", "TRANSIT"], departureDatetime: "2019-05-13 14:00:00", seed: 42, percentiles: [5, 95],
});
const reached = ttm.travel_time_p05.filter((t) => t !== peabiru.NA_INT32).length;
console.log(reached, "of", ttm.from_id.length);
```

### UnsupportedError {#UnsupportedError}

*class*

```typescript
export declare class UnsupportedError extends Error
```

The error thrown when a call asks for something peabiru does not do: an `outputDir`, an expanded or arrival matrix by a street mode alone, or a fare structure that names one of R5's own fare calculators (a `type`). peabiru never ignores an option it cannot honour.

```js
try {
  await peabiru.travelTimeMatrix(network, points, points, { outputDir: "results" });
} catch (e) {
  console.log(e instanceof peabiru.UnsupportedError, e.name);
}
```

- `constructor(message: string)`
- `readonly name: "UnsupportedError"`

## Loading the module and versions

### init {#init}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function init(input?: InitInput): Promise<void>;
```

Load and compile the WebAssembly module, once: later calls resolve at once. Without `input` the module is `pkg/peabiru_bg.wasm` next to the package (read from the file in Node, fetched elsewhere, at a URL that bundlers such as Vite and webpack 5 recognise). `input` loads it from somewhere else: a URL (string or `URL`), a `Request` or `Response`, the bytes, a compiled `WebAssembly.Module`, or a Promise of one of these. `buildNetwork()` and `getGtfsErrors()` call it themselves, so it is only needed to load the module from elsewhere, or before `coreVersion()`, `readFareStructure()` or `writeFareStructure()`.

```js
await peabiru.init(); // or: await peabiru.init(new URL("/static/peabiru_bg.wasm", location.href))
console.log(peabiru.coreVersion());
```

### initSync {#initSync}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function initSync(module: ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | WebAssembly.Module): void;
```

Load the WebAssembly module synchronously from its bytes or a compiled `WebAssembly.Module` (nothing happens when it is already loaded). Some browsers do not compile large modules synchronously on the main thread: prefer `init()` there.

```js
peabiru.initSync(await readFile("node_modules/peabiru/pkg/peabiru_bg.wasm"));
console.log(peabiru.coreVersion());
```

### InitInput {#InitInput}

*type*

```typescript
export type InitInput =
  | string
  | URL
  | Request
  | Response
  | ArrayBuffer
  | ArrayBufferView
  | WebAssembly.Module
  | Promise<Response | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | WebAssembly.Module>;
```

Where the WebAssembly module can be loaded from.

### coreVersion {#coreVersion}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function coreVersion(): string;
```

The version of the Rust routing core compiled into the module. Throws before the module is loaded (see `init()`).

```js
console.log(`package ${peabiru.version}, core ${peabiru.coreVersion()}`);
```

### version {#version}

*constant*

```typescript
export declare const version: string;
```

The version of this package, such as `"0.1.0"`.

```js
console.log(peabiru.version);
```

## Other declarations

### TripCriterion {#TripCriterion}

*type*

```typescript
export type TripCriterion = "TIME" | "FARE" | "TRANSFERS" | "WALK";
```

A criterion of `tripOptions()`.

### TripOptionsOptions {#TripOptionsOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TripOptionsOptions extends RoutingOptions
```

Also takes every option of [`RoutingOptions`](#RoutingOptions).

- `departureDatetime?: DateTime | null`: Required with public transport.
- `timeWindow?: number`: Minutes of departure, one at a time from `departureDatetime` (default 10).
- `criteria?: TripCriterion[] | TripCriterion | null`: Some of `"TIME"` (door-to-door minutes from the departure minute), `"FARE"` (needs a `fareStructure`), `"TRANSFERS"` (rides minus one; 0 without public transport) and `"WALK"` (minutes on foot: walked access and egress legs and walks between stops). Default null: all four with a `fareStructure`, all but `"FARE"` without one.
- `maxOptions?: number`: At most this many options per pair, the first in `option` order (default Infinity).
- `walkResolution?: number`: Seconds to which minutes on foot are compared (default 60: the whole minute, rounded), so that of two trips a few seconds of walking apart and otherwise no better only one is returned; 1 compares the exact seconds.
- `allToAll?: boolean`: Route from every origin to every destination (default false: pair them row by row).
- `itineraries?: boolean`: Build the legs of each option (default true).
- `byDeparture?: boolean`: Add the options of every departure minute (default false).
- `fareStructure?: FareStructure | null`: A fare structure (default null): needed for the `"FARE"` criterion, gives every option its fare.
- `maxFare?: number`: The highest fare of a trip (default Infinity).
- `dropGeometry?: boolean`: Plain rows for the legs instead of GeoJSON features (default false).
- `osmLinkIds?: boolean`: Add r5r's `osm_link_ids` properties to each leg (default false), as in `detailedItineraries()`.

### TripOptionRow {#TripOptionRow}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TripOptionRow
```

One option of a pair: trips with the same street modes, the same routes between the same stops and the same fare, transfers and minutes on foot, not dominated at `n_departures` departure minutes. Times are those of its best minute (the least total time); minutes have one decimal.

- `from_id: string | null`
- `to_id: string | null`
- `option: number`: From 1, ordered by total time, then fare, transfers and minutes on foot.
- `total_time: number`
- `fare?: number`: With a fare structure only.
- `transfers: number`
- `walk_time: number`
- `departure_time: string`
- `arrival_time: string`
- `n_departures: number`
- `first_departure: string`
- `last_departure: string`
- `description: string`: The modes and route short names, as `"WALK > BUS 343 > WALK"`.

### TripDepartureRow {#TripDepartureRow}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TripDepartureRow
```

One option on the frontier of one departure minute (`byDeparture`).

- `from_id: string | null`
- `to_id: string | null`
- `option: number`
- `departure_time: string`
- `arrival_time: string`
- `total_time: number`

### TripLegRow {#TripLegRow}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TripLegRow
```

One leg of an option, keyed by `from_id`, `to_id` and `option`, in the format of `detailedItineraries()`.

- `from_id: string | null`
- `to_id: string | null`
- `option: number`
- `segment: number`
- `mode: string`
- `cumulative_fare?: number`: With a fare structure only: the fare paid up to the end of the leg.
- `segment_duration: number`
- `wait: number`
- `distance: number`
- `route: string`
- `osm_id_list?: string`
- `edge_id_list?: string`
- `board_stop_id?: string`
- `alight_stop_id?: string`

### TripLegFeature {#TripLegFeature}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TripLegFeature
```

A leg of an option with its line (longitude, latitude), as a GeoJSON feature.

- `type: "Feature"`
- `properties: TripLegRow`
- `geometry: { type: "LineString"; coordinates: [number, number][] }`

### TripOptions {#TripOptions}

*interface*

```typescript
export interface TripOptions
```

The result of `tripOptions()`.

- `options: TripOptionRow[]`
- `itineraries: { type: "FeatureCollection"; features: TripLegFeature[] } | TripLegRow[] | null`: The legs (null with `itineraries: false`).
- `departures: TripDepartureRow[] | null`: Every minute's options (null without `byDeparture`).

### tripOptions {#tripOptions}

*function*

```typescript
export declare function tripOptions(
  network: Network,
  origins: Points,
  destinations: Points,
  options?: TripOptionsOptions,
): Promise<TripOptions>;
```

peabiru's own multi-criteria trip planner (r5r has no counterpart): for each origin-destination pair, the trips that no other trip beats on all the chosen criteria at once, at each departure minute of the window, merged into options. Frequency-based routes are boarded at their expected times (half a headway): no random draws. See the guide "Trip options".

```js
const res = await peabiru.tripOptions(network, { id: ["a"], lon: [-46.6290], lat: [-23.5563] },
  { id: ["c"], lon: [-46.6355], lat: [-23.5601] }, {
    departureDatetime: "2019-05-13 14:00:00", timeWindow: 3, itineraries: false,
  });
console.log(res.options.map((o) => `${o.total_time} min, ${o.walk_time} on foot: ${o.description}`));
```
